rounds.hypothesis: diagnose.json's root cause read directly: the signal number is a compile-time constant baked into one shared closure, and PosixTimerManager::new clones that single WorkItem into all three interval timers, so ITIMER_VIRTUAL and ITIMER_PROF can only ever enqueue SIGALRM. The signal identity belongs to the individual timer, so parameterizing the factory and binding a signal per timer at construction should make all three types deliver their own signal.
rounds.change: kernel/src/process/process/timer_manager.rs: gave create_process_timer_callback a `signum: SigNum` parameter, used it at the KernelSignal::new site in place of the hardcoded SIGALRM, and imported SIGVTALRM/SIGPROF and SigNum alongside SIGALRM. Replaced the single `let callback = ...` plus two .clone()s in PosixTimerManager::new with one factory call per timer - SIGALRM for alarm_timer, SIGVTALRM for virtual_timer, SIGPROF for prof_timer - so the three timers own three independent WorkItems instead of aliasing one. Dropped the now-unused `+ Clone` bound from the factory's return type, since nothing clones the callback anymore. Enabled setitimer01 by uncommenting testcases/all.txt:1436.
rounds.outcome: green: qemu.log line 43 'setitimer01: pass (3.583s)', 18 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken / 0 skipped, matching the 18/18 host baseline exactly (was 16/2 before). Regression boot over alarm03, alarm05, alarm06, alarm07, getitimer01, getitimer02, setitimer01, setitimer02 and timer_create03 also all pass, 64 assertions, 0 failed - so SIGALRM delivery via sys_alarm and ITIMER_REAL is intact and POSIX timers are unaffected. Re-verified after removing the Clone bound: cargo check clean, and the 9-test regression boot green again.

layer: The process timer-management layer, exactly the owning_layer diagnose named: PosixTimerManager in kernel/src/process/process/timer_manager.rs and its create_process_timer_callback factory. This is the only place the timer-type-to-signal association can be established. Below it, the timer core (time/core/timer.rs) is generic over Fn(TimerGuard) and process_expired_timers calls callback.call() with no information about which timer it belongs to; above it, sys_setitimer only selects an already-constructed timer. Nothing in the timer core, the syscall entry, or the signal layer was touched.
generalizes: The fix binds the signal at timer construction for every process, not on the path this test walks - there is no branch on which, on the test's flags, or on any value the test supplies, and the factory body is now signal-agnostic. It makes the invariant structural rather than conditional: because each of the three create_timer calls gets its own WorkItem, timers of different types can no longer alias one expiry action at all, which is the aliasing bug itself and not just its symptom. On other callers: create_process_timer_callback has exactly one caller in the tree, so the blast radius is the three timers it builds. alarm_timer is the one with outside consumers - sys_alarm (syscall/alarm.rs:14) arms it and procfs pid/task/stat.rs:201 reads its remaining time - and it keeps SIGALRM because SIGALRM is now passed explicitly rather than removed; verified green via alarm03/05/06/07. virtual_timer and prof_timer are reached only by sys_setitimer/sys_getitimer plus the internal CPU-clock tick sites, and nothing depended on the old wrong signal. The separate create_prof_timer/create_virtual_timer methods take their callback from the caller and serve timer_create, so POSIX timers are untouched; timer_create03 confirms. Honest scope note: no third-party caller sees this bug today, so the fix is narrow - but the correctness argument is that SIGVTALRM and SIGPROF now have their first senders in the kernel, where before they were defined, ordered for delivery, and named, yet constructed nowhere.
fix_summary: Process interval timers now raise the signal that belongs to their own type - ITIMER_REAL/SIGALRM, ITIMER_VIRTUAL/SIGVTALRM, ITIMER_PROF/SIGPROF - by making the signal a parameter of the callback factory and binding it per timer at construction. Designed against Asterinas's own abstractions rather than transplanting Linux's structure: Linux keeps the signal out of the timer state entirely and passes signo per call site into check_cpu_itimer, and the equivalent enforcement point here is the Weak<Process> callback factory that PosixTimerManager::new feeds to TimerManager::create_timer, since Asterinas's timer core is a generic Fn(TimerGuard) with no notion of signals. I kept the existing cached-WorkItem design (one work item built per timer, resubmitted on each expiry) instead of the alternative of routing through process::enqueue_signal_async, which already takes a SigNum and would have shortened the callback to a line: these timers re-arm on an interval and fire repeatedly, and enqueue_signal_async's submit_work_func allocates a fresh work item per expiry, so switching would have traded a real hot-path allocation for cosmetic brevity. The only structural change is that three independent work items replace three handles to one aliased work item, which is what makes the per-type signal possible.
